title: Shinnecock Powwow Grounds
summary: Formally organized in 1946, the Shinnecock Powwow is a decades long traditional and cultural celebration that takes place on the Shinnecock Indian Reservation. Every year on Labor Day weekend, the Powwow takes place on Shinnecock and is open to the public. The annual four-day Shinnecock Labor Day Powwow attracts more than 15,000 attendees each day and serves as both a cultural focal point and fundraiser for the Nation. The Powwow began as historical 'pageants' that took place throughout Southampton Town,.

activity_pin_preview: The Shinnecock Nation hosts the 80th Annual Shinnecock Powwow on Labor Day Weekend, September 4-7, 2026, at the Shinnecock Powwow Grounds, 100 Montauk Hwy, Southampton. Source: Shinnecock Nation annual powwow page.
activity_update_summary: Kept Hunter's disputed 1936 fundraiser account in the cited Historic Timeline and removed the duplicate article section.
why_this_matters: Formally organized in 1946 and now attracting over 15,000 daily visitors every Labor Day weekend, the Shinnecock Powwow serves as a massive, vibrant celebration of Indigenous cultural endurance. By welcoming the public to share in these living traditions, the Shinnecock Nation challenges myths of Native disappearance and reinforces their unbroken sovereignty on their ancestral homeland.
preservation_content:
The Southampton Rogers Memorial Library preserves a digital collection of Powwow Programs from 1955 to current; myrml.org

1950s Shinnecock Powwow photograph

A 1950s Shinnecock Powwow photograph from the project archive gives visual context for mid-twentieth-century public cultural presence at Shinnecock. It supports the longer history of powwow gathering, community visibility, and cultural continuance.

Source: Shinnecock Powwow photograph, 1950s, project archive / Shinnecock Archaeology and History Drive folder.
